keyVerseText: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the LORD. in process: Heb. at the end of days
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun קֵץ (qêts) derives from the root קָצַץ (qâtsats), which means to cut off or sever. This etymology highlights the concept of an extremity or boundary being literally 'cut off' or ended, giving the word a vivid sense of finality beyond the abstract English term 'end.' The root’s notion of cutting emphasizes a definitive and often abrupt termination, whether in time or space.
usageInScripture: Throughout its 67 occurrences, קֵץ consistently conveys the idea of an end or boundary, especially in relation to time. It is frequently translated as 'at the end,' 'after,' or 'an end,' demonstrating its function as a temporal marker signaling the conclusion of a period or process. This consistent usage underlines the word's role in expressing both concrete endpoints and the unfolding of events to their destined conclusion.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding קֵץ as a word rooted in the idea of cutting off enriches our grasp of biblical eschatology and divine timing. It reminds believers that God’s sovereign plan includes appointed ends and boundaries, whether for individual lives, peoples, or cosmic history. This word anchors the Christian hope in the certainty of God’s ultimate purposes being fulfilled, encouraging faithfulness in the present as we await the consummation of all things in Christ. It also serves as a sober reminder of judgment and the finality of God’s righteous decrees.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 4:3 states, 'And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the LORD,' with the phrase 'in process' literally meaning 'at the end of days.' Here, קֵץ conveys the unfolding of God’s timing in the early narrative of human history. It emphasizes that events occur according to divine appointment, reinforcing that even ordinary moments like Cain’s offering happen within God’s sovereignly determined framework of time.
